user_stories.story: As the maintainer, I want the 912-line backend/tests/test_logs.py split into topic files (conftest, api, http_responses, logs, photos, validation, database) so each file is short and findable.
As the maintainer, I want every existing test to behave exactly as before (same name, body, parametrization, assertions) and the same test command to work.
As the maintainer, I want a few short end-to-end workflow tests in test_api.py using only the public API.
As the maintainer, I want the guard that proves the real logs.db and uploads/ are never touched to keep running for the whole session.

acceptance_criteria.c: Files in backend/tests/ after the change: conftest.py, test_api.py, test_http_responses.py, test_logs.py, test_photos.py, test_validation.py, test_database.py. Nothing outside backend/tests/ is created, modified or deleted (production code, frontend/, real logs.db, uploads/ unchanged). No __pycache__ or .pytest_cache is left under the project.

The command `cd backend && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 ../.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests` passes with no failures or errors. The count is 130 + N passed, where N is the number of new test_api.py tests, 1 <= N <= 3 (so 131 to 133). Warnings: the same single warning as baseline or fewer.

Moved tests: each of the 75 existing test functions (130 collected items counting parametrization) appears in exactly one file, the one in the mapping below, and in no other. Name, body, decorators, parameter lists and assertions are unchanged. Only the import/helper-reference lines and the surrounding file layout may differ. Collected node ids for each moved function (including parametrization ids) are identical to baseline apart from the file prefix. `pytest --collect-only -q` shows exactly 130 + N items.
test_logs.py remains and contains only the tests the mapping assigns to it. The tests it loses are removed from it.

conftest.py contains: the sys.dont_write_bytecode / sys.path setup (backend dir inserted so `import main`, `models`, `database` work), the `env` fixture (unchanged), the session-scoped autouse `_real_paths_guard` fixture with its `_real_state()` and `_REAL_BEFORE` snapshot taken at conftest import time, and the shared helpers per criterion 7. conftest.py contains no test_* functions.

test_real_paths_untouched exists in test_database.py, unchanged, and passes. It compares against the same `_REAL_BEFORE` object the session guard uses (a single conftest module instance, not a second copy). The guard still fails the session if logs.db or uploads/ metadata changes; the guard fixture is session autouse, so it applies to every test file without being imported by them.

Helper sharing rule: a helper or constant used by two or more test files is defined once in conftest.py and imported by test files with `from conftest import ...`. A helper or constant used by exactly one file is defined in that file. Helpers affected: make_image, post, put, rows, snapshot, make_log, assert_nothing_stored are shared (conftest). MAX, padded_png, TOO_LONG are validation-only. post_old is http-responses-only. file_bytes and SHAPE are test_logs.py-only, unless a new test_api.py test also uses them, in which case they go to conftest. Each helper is defined in exactly one place (no duplicate definitions across files). No new helpers module exists, and no helper bodies are changed.

Every test file imports cleanly on its own: `pytest tests/test_X.py` passes for each of the seven files taken alone (test_api.py with its new tests; every other file with its mapped tests, including test_real_paths_untouched in test_database.py). No unused imports in any file (flake8 F401 clean, if available; otherwise manual check). PEP 8 style and the existing comment density, naming and `# noqa: E402` convention are kept.

test_api.py has 1 to 3 new tests, each under about 25 lines, using only HTTP calls through the `env` fixture or create_app/TestClient and the shared helpers. No monkeypatching and no direct DB/file inspection except to compare the db and uploads paths passed to create_app. It must include (a) a lifecycle test: create -> list -> edit -> list -> delete -> list, asserting the status codes (201, 200, 200, 200, 204, 200) and the list contents at each step; and (b) a restart test: create a log with a photo, build a second create_app on the same db_path and uploads_dir, and assert the log is listed with identical JSON and the photo is retrievable at its returned URL. A third test is optional. These are the only new tests. No existing test is modified in behavior.
No test file exceeds 400 lines (target: under about 300). Each file's header docstring is a one-line description matching the user's layout descriptions.
No test is skipped, xfailed, deselected or weakened (no changed assert, no removed parametrize value). The implementation record lists the test -> file mapping.

mapping.check: Totals: 14 + 16 + 30 + 6 + 9 = 75 moved functions; items 16 + 31 + 67 + 7 + 9 = 130. The function-to-file assignment is binding; the verifier recomputes per-file item counts from --collect-only and confirms they match these numbers.

assumptions.a: The "130 tests" are pytest items; there are 75 test functions. The mapping is by function name and carries parametrization with it.

Helpers stay in conftest.py and are imported with `from conftest import ...`. Reason: pytest (default prepend import mode, tests/ has no __init__.py) puts tests/ on sys.path, so conftest is importable as the single module `conftest`. That is the same module instance pytest loaded, so `_REAL_BEFORE` is not duplicated. This needs no extra module, and turning plain helpers into fixtures would force every call site to change (violating the "body unchanged" rule). A separate helpers.py is not needed.
Single-file helpers live in their only consumer file (criterion 7) to keep conftest small. If the implementer finds a helper is actually used in two files, it moves to conftest.

Placement judgment calls: tests of the 500/rollback paths on the DB go to test_database.py; disk-error and file-cleanup tests go to test_photos.py; all request-rejection tests (422/413) including PUT variants go to test_validation.py; upload traversal and absolute-path refusals count as image serving (test_photos.py). test_real_paths_untouched must live in a test_*.py file because pytest does not collect tests from conftest.py.
Line limits (criterion 10) are checked against the file as written. test_validation.py is the largest and may approach 300 lines. That is accepted up to 400.

edge_cases.e: Collection order change must not alter results: no test depends on another test's state (each uses tmp_path via env). The session guard still wraps all files.
test_hostile_filenames_stay_in_uploads and the traversal tests take tmp_path along with env, and still work after the move.

monkeypatch targets (`database.insert_log`, `database.update_log`, `database.delete_log`, "builtins.open", "os.remove") require `import database` in the files that use them, and the same module object as the app uses.
Tests that call create_app directly need `from main import create_app` and `TestClient` imports in those files.
Windows: no leftover temp files, and the restart test opens two TestClient contexts sequentially (not nested) on the same tmp paths.

risks.risk: Importing helpers from `conftest` could create two module copies if the import mode differs (for example `--import-mode=importlib`). The guard's `_REAL_BEFORE` would then differ between copies. The fixed test command uses the default mode, so it is not triggered. Mitigated by criterion 6.
A moved test silently loses an import (for example `database`, `sqlite3`, `Path`) and fails only when its file is run alone. Mitigated by criterion 8.
Judgment-based placement may be disputed by the user. The mapping is explicit and easy to move.
The restart test depends on create_app startup being idempotent on an existing db. If it fails because of a production bug, the implementer must report it, not alter production code.

spec.dependencies: pytest, fastapi.testclient, Pillow, existing backend modules main/models/database (read-only), .venv/Scripts/python.exe.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: split (1,4,10), unchanged behavior (2,3,11), workflow tests (9), guard (5,6). Each criterion is mechanically checkable via --collect-only, per-file runs, line counts and grep. The biggest uncertainty is the topic placement of borderline tests (the user's categories overlap), which the explicit mapping fixes. A secondary one is the "130 tests" wording, which means items, not functions. No blocking ambiguity remains, so there are no clarifications.
